limitations: Single 16-item same-KB holdout run, not a multi-run statistical study.
Baseline after-resume metrics are human-assisted and should not replace first-pass robustness metrics.
Baseline h016 timed out on three consecutive attempts; partial resume files contain duplicate h016 rows, so metrics must be computed from main JSONL outputs keyed by id.
Tuned latency regressed substantially while robustness and groundedness improved.
The adjusted 697b275 cleanup reused this holdout to verify router and latency changes; the 16-item holdout is now burned and should be treated only as a regression artifact, not fresh validation.
The cd6c0ef prompt-invariant route probe is route-only evidence on the already-burned holdout; it does not rescore retrieval, answer quality, groundedness, or latency.

interpretation.headline: The 36-item tuning partially reproduced on the fresh 16-item holdout: transport robustness and groundedness reproduced; routing and broad semantic correctness did not cleanly reproduce; latency regressed.
interpretation.baseline_timeout_is_signal: Baseline retries only HTTP 429/500/503/504; tuned additionally retries requests Timeout and ConnectionError. First-pass baseline timeouts are therefore a real robustness gap, not rows to symmetrically exclude.
interpretation.next_step: Use a new holdout for future tuning decisions. Treat h011 and h015 from the burned set as regression/debugging signals only.
